Link.description:
The other pages, as `<url>; rel="prev"`, `"next"`, `"first"` and
`"last"`. `prev` is absent on the first page and `next` on the last.
Follow these URLs rather than building your own; they keep the
request's other query parameters.

X-CodePen-Partial.description: Sent with the `block` filter only. `true` when the scan stopped before finding a full page.

collectionId.description: The Collection's hashid, the id in its URL.
collectionId.name: id

dry_run.description:
Build the proposed files without saving them: the head does not move
and the answer's `version` has `saved: false`. A `dry_run` in the JSON
body takes precedence.
dry_run.name: dry_run

expected_version_id.description:
The `saved_version.id` the change was built on. The write is refused
with `409` if the Pen's head has moved since.
expected_version_id.name: expected_version_id

filePath.description:
The file's full path in the Pen, without the leading `/`. Its
slashes may be sent as they are (`src/app.js`) or encoded
(`src%2Fapp.js`, as OpenAPI clients encode a path parameter).
filePath.name: path

penId.description:
The Pen's cpid or hashid, or a CodePen URL that names the Pen (editor,
pen or preview URL).
penId.name: id

per_page.description: Items per page. A value over 100 is reduced to 100, not refused.
per_page.name: per_page

sort.description: The order: by creation or update time.
sort.name: sort

sortPens.description: The order: by creation or update time, by popularity, or by title.
sortPens.name: sort

sortPopularity.description: The order: by creation or update time, or by popularity.
sortPopularity.name: sort

wait.description:
Seconds to wait for the build (default 45, at most 75; `0` answers as
soon as the files are saved). A `wait` in the JSON body takes
precedence.
wait.name: wait

example.message: per_page must be a positive number

BadRequest.description:
`BAD_USER_INPUT`: an invalid parameter, body, path, setting, access
level or role. `field` names the argument when known, and `details`
carries structured detail (the misses of `PATCH /v2/pens/{id}/files`).

BuildTimeout.description:
`BUILD_TIMEOUT`: a dry run's build did not finish inside `wait`, and
there is no saved version to poll. Retry with a longer `wait`.

example.message: the Pen's head is 01a0...c5, not 01a0...99; read it again and retry

Conflict.description: `CONFLICT`: `expected_version_id` is no longer the Pen's head. Read the Pen again and retry.

FilesWrite.description: The Pen, the newest version the write produced with its `files`, and that version's build.

Forbidden.description:
`FORBIDDEN`: a write to a Pen made in the classic editor, or a plan
limit (non-Public access, a Private Collection, file size, storage,
collaborators). The message names the limit and, when a bigger plan
would lift it, where to upgrade.

Internal.description: `INTERNAL`: unexpected, and reported; the message is generic.

NotFound.description:
`NOT_FOUND`: no such item, or one that is not the key owner's, public
or not. A path that is not an endpoint at all answers `404` with the
v1 body `{ "error": "not found" }` instead.

example.message: daily limit reached: the Free plan allows 5 Pens a day through the API. Upgrade to PRO for 150 a day at https://codepen.io/pricing

RateLimited.description:
`RATE_LIMITED`: the owner exceeded the plan's requests in an hour, its
reads today, or today's allowance of Pen or Collection creates. No
`Retry-After` or rate-limit headers are sent; the body carries
`retry_after_seconds`, `limit` and `reset_at`.

Unauthorized.description: `UNAUTHENTICATED`: a missing or invalid key, a deleted owner, or a Team key for a Team that is not PRO.

is_binary.description:
Text Assets are those with a text extension: SVG,
HTML/HAML/Pug/Slim/Markdown, CSS/Sass/SCSS/Less/Stylus,
JS/JSX/TS/TSX/CoffeeScript/JSON/source maps, Vue, GLSL and plain
text. Everything else is binary.

AssetFilename.description: At most 191 bytes, unique among the owner's Assets, without `/` or `\`.

content.description: Text Assets only; send binary files as a multipart `file` part.
A text Asset's content; null for a binary one, whose bytes are served at `url`.

applied_patches.description: Changes the API applied to the caller's files on the compiler's behalf.

diagnostics.description: Every diagnostic of the final build.

files.description:
The compiled output served under the version's `preview_url`. On
the single version and build endpoints and the writes, and only
when the build succeeded.

id.description: The version's id, before and after the version is saved.

next_id.description: The build applying this one's patches.

previous_id.description: The caller's build this one was converged from.

rounds.description: How many compiler builds it took, counted from the version the caller wrote.

status.description: `Canceled` means changes are still required; see `patches` and `next_id`.

version_id.description: Null while the version is still being converged.
The version to deploy; the saved head when omitted.

build_id.description: On `BUILD_TIMEOUT`, the build to poll when it has an id.

details.description: On `BAD_USER_INPUT`, structured detail about it, such as the `misses` of a hunk edit.

field.description: On `BAD_USER_INPUT`, the argument it is about, when known.

reset_at.description: On `RATE_LIMITED`, when the counter resets, when known.

retry_after_seconds.description: On `RATE_LIMITED`, seconds until the counter resets.

content.description: Null for binary files, which are read from `url`.

content_type.description: The media type the file is served with, from its extension.

download_url.description:
The file's exact bytes for anyone holding the URL, on the API host
(`GET /v2/pens/{id}/download/{path}`), for one hour from this
response: no API key, session or Referer needed. Served as an
attachment with the file's `content_type`. A new URL comes with
every read; an expired one answers `403`. Null for the files of a
Pen made in the classic editor.

id.description: Stable across versions, renames and edits.

url.description:
Where the file is served raw on the Pen's content domain. It
follows the Pen's own access rules: a Private, Protected or
Collaborators Pen needs a browser session and a Pen owned by a
Free account needs a CodePen Referer, neither of which an API
client has, so read files through `content` or `download_url`.
Null for the files of a Pen made in the classic editor.

FileChange.description: Addresses a file by `path` or `id`; see the operation's table.

id.description: The file, by id. One of `id` and `path`. Text files only.

new.description: The replacement. An empty string deletes the matched text.

old.description: Text that appears in the file exactly once, byte for byte.

path.description: The file, by full path. One of `id` and `path`.

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence of `old` instead of requiring exactly one.

content.description: Text only; send a binary file as a multipart `file` part.

build.description:
Only on `POST /v2/pens` and `POST /v2/pens/{id}/fork`: the first
version's build, or the converged version's when the compiler asked
for changes.

editor.description: `V2`, or `Classic` for a Pen made in the classic editor, which is read-only through the API.

id.description: The cpid, or the hashid for a Pen made in the classic editor.

saved_version.description: The Pen's head, without `files`; null for a Pen made in the classic editor.

screenshot_urls.description: Screenshots of the saved head; null for a Pen with no saved version.

views_count.description: Views as the site shows them, tallied in batches, so it can trail by a few minutes.

PenAccess.description:
`Public`; `Private` (not listed on the site; anyone with the link can
view it); `Protected` (private and password protected); `Collaborators`
(private and for collaborators only). Anything but `Public` needs a PRO
plan.

password.description: Required with `Protected` access, and refused with any other.

tags.description: Optional; up to 5 tags, each 2 to 50 characters of letters, digits and dashes (stored lowercase, spaces as dashes).

a_record.description: What the last lookup found for the A record, such as `None`, `Valid`, `Legacy` or `Invalid`.

cname_record.description: What the last lookup found for the CNAME record, such as `None`, `Valid`, `Legacy` or `Invalid`.

dns.description: The records to create for the host to verify.

content.description: Text only; binary files go up as multipart parts.

tags.description: Up to 5 tags, each 2 to 50 characters of letters, digits and dashes; defaults to the original's.

password.description:
Required when changing to `Protected`. On a Pen that is already
Protected, `password` alone replaces the password.

tags.description: Replaces the whole list; up to 5 tags, each 2 to 50 characters of letters, digits and dashes. An empty list clears them.

preview.description:
Renders the saved head on its own; 404s for Protected and
Collaborators Pens, which need a browser session.

RouteNotFoundError.description: The v1 error body, answered for a path that is not an endpoint.

ScreenshotUrls.description:
JPEG screenshots of the saved head, 16:9, by width. A screenshot is
rendered the first time it is requested, so the first fetch can take a
few seconds.

item_id.description: The Pen's or Collection's id, for the restore endpoints.

Upload.description: A file's bytes, as one part of a multipart form.

files.description: The version's source files; only on `GET /v2/versions/{id}` and the file writes.

preview_url.description: Null for a dry run's version, or when the key cannot read the Pen.

saved.description: False only for a dry run's unsaved version.

Wait.description: Seconds to wait for the build (default 45, at most 75; `0` answers as soon as the files are saved).

dry_run.description:
Build the proposed files without saving them. The head does not
move, and the answer's `version` has `saved: false`; it stays
readable at `GET /v2/versions/{id}` for 36 hours.

expected_version_id.description:
The `saved_version.id` the change was built on. The write is refused
with `409` if the Pen's head has moved since.

bearerKey.description: An API key from Settings → API on codepen.io.

headerKey.description: The same API key, in a header of its own.
headerKey.name: X-API-Key

info.description:
The v2 REST API on `api.codepen.io`: JSON over HTTP with snake_case keys.

CodePen also has a **GraphQL API** with the same operations at
`POST /v2/graphql`. Both run the same logic and take the same keys, so
use whichever suits your client. See the
[GraphQL API docs](https://blog.codepen.io/docs/api/api-v2/graphql-api-v2/).

Every request carries an API key, as `Authorization: Bearer cp_user_...`
or `X-API-Key: cp_user_...`. A key belongs to a User (`cp_user_`) or a Team
(`cp_team_`), and everything it lists, reads, creates or changes belongs to
that key owner. Another User's or Team's Pen or Collection is not found,
even when it is public.

Conventions:

- Enum values are accepted in any case in requests; responses use the
  PascalCase spelling shown here.
- Timestamps are RFC 3339 in UTC. Ids are the ids in CodePen URLs.
- Write endpoints take a JSON body, or `multipart/form-data` when they
  upload files. Unknown keys are ignored. A JSON body is capped at 16 MB,
  a multipart request at 120 MB and one file at 30 MB.
- Endpoints that create answer `201`; endpoints that remove something and
  have nothing to return answer `204`.
- Lists are JSON arrays paged with `page` and `per_page` and a `Link`
  header, the way GitHub's REST API pages.

Errors are `{ "message", "code" }` with recovery fields beside the code
when they apply. No `Retry-After` or rate-limit headers are sent; a
`RATE_LIMITED` body carries `retry_after_seconds`, `limit` and `reset_at`
instead.

The frozen, read-only v1 API (`/v1/pens/:id` and
`/v1/collections/:id/pens`) is not described here; see
https://blog.codepen.io/docs/api/rest-api-v1/.

A version's build, by the version's id: the write's `build.id`, or

but `Public` needs a PRO plan.

The answer is the Pen with the first version's `build`; `wait` in the
body or the query bounds how long the request waits for it.

`pen` is the JSON body. Every other part is one uploaded file,
named by its path in the Pen (`/img/logo.png`).

`GET /v2/trash`, and can be restored for three days.

The metadata is saved first and the access change second, so a refused
access change leaves the metadata saved.

get.description:
The route a file's `download_url` points at. The URL names one file's
exact bytes (the Pen, the content `hash` and the path) and carries an
expiry and a signature over all of it, so anyone holding it fetches
the file for an hour with no API key, session or Referer. Read the
file through the API for a URL; the parameters are not meant to be
built by hand. The bytes are served as an attachment with the file's
`content_type`. A URL for a Pen that has since been moved to the
trash answers `404`.

parameters.description: The file's `content_hash`.
parameters.name: hash

parameters.description: When the URL stops answering, as unix seconds.
parameters.name: expires

parameters.description: The signature over the Pen, hash, path and expiry.
parameters.name: sig

200.description: The file's bytes, as an attachment.

example.message: the download link has expired; read the file again for a new one

403.description: `FORBIDDEN`: the URL has expired. Read the file again for a new one.

404.description: `NOT_FOUND`: the signature does not match the Pen, hash and path, or the Pen or its owner is gone.

get.summary: Download a file through its signed URL

get.description: The files of the saved head, with `content`.

patch.description:
Changes text files without resending them. Each hunk names a file and
replaces `old`, text that appears in it exactly once, with `new`. Hunks
are applied in order, each against the result of the ones before it,
and every file they touch is written as one saved version.

A hunk whose `old` matches nowhere byte for byte, but matches exactly
one run of whole lines once leading indentation is ignored, is applied
to those lines and `new` is re-indented to match.

Nothing is applied by halves: one hunk that cannot be applied fails the
whole write with `400 BAD_USER_INPUT`, `field` `edits`, and
`details.misses` listing every miss (`index`, `path`, `reason` of
`NotFound`, `Ambiguous` or `NoSuchFile`, and `matches`, `lines` or
`nearest` to retry with). A set of hunks that changes nothing is
refused.

put.description:
Applies `files` changes, in order, as one saved version and builds it.
Each change addresses a file by `path` or `id`:

| Change | Effect |
| --- | --- |
| `{ path, content }` | Writes the file at `path`, creating it if needed. |
| `{ id, content }` | Writes the file with that id, wherever it is. |
| `{ id, path }` | Moves the file to `path`; it keeps its id. Add `content` to write there too. |
| `{ path, delete: true }` | Deletes the file, or every file under a directory path. |
| `{ id, delete: true }` | Deletes the file with that id. |

Binary files go up as parts of a multipart form, each one more change
applied after those in `changes`.

schema.description:
`changes` is the JSON body. Every other part is one uploaded
file, named by its path in the Pen.

requestBody.description: The changes as JSON, or a multipart form whose `changes` part is that JSON and whose other parts are files.

delete.description:
A directory path deletes every file under it. The answer is the new
version, not `204`. Deleting by id goes through `PUT /v2/pens/{id}/files`
with `{ "id": "...", "delete": true }`.
delete.summary: Delete one file or a directory

requestBody.description: Text `content` as JSON, or a multipart `file` part.

One version with its `files`, and its `build` with output files. A dry

tags.description:
A Pen's source files, written as one saved version per request and built
by the compiler. A Pen made in the classic editor has files that can be
read but not written.
tags.name: Files

tags.description:
Every write saves the caller's files as a version and builds it. When the
compiler needs the files to change before it can build them, the API
applies those changes, builds again and saves the result as one more
version. Writes wait for the build (`wait`, default 45 seconds, at most
75, `0` to answer as soon as the files are saved); a build still running
afterwards is polled at `GET /v2/builds/{id}`.
tags.name: Builds
